title: 2018 AMC 12A Problem 14
statement: The solution to the equation \(\log_{3x} 4 = \log_{2x} 8,\) where \(x\) is a positive real number other than \(\tfrac13\) or \(\tfrac12,\) can be written as \(\tfrac{p}{q},\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is \(p + q?\)

solutions.text:
Writing both logarithms in base \(2:\) \(\tfrac{2}{\log_2 3x} = \tfrac{3}{\log_2 2x},\) so \(2 \log_2 2x = 3 \log_2 3x,\) i.e. \((2x)^2 = (3x)^3.\) Then \(4x^2 = 27x^3,\) giving \(x = \tfrac{4}{27}.\) Since \(\gcd(4, 27) = 1,\) we get \(p + q = 4 + 27 = 31.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Rewrite both sides with a common base: \(\log_{3x} 4 = \tfrac{\log 4}{\log 3x},\) and similarly for \(\log_{2x} 8\)
Cross-multiplying reduces the equation to \((2x)^2 = (3x)^3;\) solve for \(x\) as a reduced fraction
